text:
incident-bot: Pager fired -> INC-4321: p99 latency breach for service=\"inference-gateway-us-west\" (p99 > 2.0s). Alert rule: telemetry.latency.p99 > 2s for 5m. runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/latency-tail.

pagerduty: Incident INC-4321 created and assigned to @james (primary). Priority: P1. Link: https://pd/redwood/INC-4321

james: ack. I'm on it. pulling up traces + hotkeys. will update in ~2 mins.

nina: ack from backup. if you need handoff I can take after 20m.

james: quick snapshot — p99 jumped ~12:02 UTC from ~380ms -> 2.1s, sustained. p50/p90 unchanged. no error-rate spike. looks like tail latency, maybe KV cache thrash. query used: 
```
sum(rate(kv_evictions[5m])) by (node)
```
shows eviction rate x4 on sidecar nodes in us-west-1a.

maya: thanks. suppressing autopager while we debug to avoid noisy escalations. executing: `/incident suppress-autopager 30m --reason \"investigating p99 tail\"` :hourglass:

pagerduty: autopager suppressed for 30m (requested by @maya).

james: proposal: two quick mitigations — 1) scale sidecar pool by +2 replicas to reduce eviction pressure, 2) route a small % (5-10%) to model-quantized-v1 fallback (lower memory KV working set). prefer (1) first for minimal regression risk.

nina: if you're going to scale, lmk the kubectl patch, I'll run it if you're busy.

james: running scale now.
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment sidecar-cache-usw --replicas=6
```
(I bumped from 4 -> 6)

ops-bot: Autoscaler event: +2 replicas requested for deployment/sidecar-cache-usw. Rolling update starting. Nodes available: 3 -> 5.

james: seeing p99 drop to ~980ms after pods started (12:07 UTC). still above target but trending. good sign.

maya: do we need to route traffic / apply fallback? if p99 stays >1s for another 10m we should failover to quantized model per runbook.

james: agree. prepping route. sample command if needed: 
```
POST /routing/v1/set-fallback
{"service":"inference-gateway-us-west","percent":10,"variant":"model-quantized-v1"}
```

nina: customer-impact check — top talkers table shows ~9% of requests in last 5m hit >2s. top affected customer: acme-enterprise (10% of their requests timed out on long generation calls). support-ticket queue shows spike but no escalations yet. cc: @sre-rotation for potential ops outreach.

sre-rotation: noted. I'll loop in solutions-eng for customer comms if we need to notify. hold until we confirm persistent >=2m impact.

james: running a small cache-warm script to prime hot keys (best-effort) — will run once. snippet: 
```
python tools/prime_kv.py --service inference-gateway-us-west --topn 5000
```
This should reduce cold-miss tail.

ops-bot: prime_kv job initiated (job-id=prime-1755551234). ETA ~45s.

james: p99 now ~720ms for last 2m (12:10-12:12). still watching for stabilization. marking incident timeline in PD.

maya: nice. any config changes made? note in PD: scaled sidecars, primed keys, suppressed autopager.

james: added notes to PD, will handoff to @nina in 15m. keep autopager suppressed until we're stable. if p99 <= 700ms for 10m we can resolve, otherwise escalate to platform infra (tag: infra-latency).

nina: taking handoff at 12:25 UTC. thanks @james — will continue checks and watch for regressions. I'll also keep an eye on acme-enterprise and notify support if their error-rate doesn't recover.

incident-bot: Reminder: incident has active mitigation steps. Runbook state = Mitigating. Next checkpoint in 10m.

james: handing off now to @nina — brief: scaled sidecar +2, primed KV for top keys, autopager suppressed, watching p99. details in PD notes. I'm available if anything spikes back up. :white_check_mark:

nina: ack, taking over. setting PD to manual-ack and adding timeline note.

pagerduty: Incident status updated: assigned to nina (handed off). Manual ack mode enabled.

ops-bot: monitoring: p99 12:12-12:18 window = 610ms average, eviction-rate trending down. Will alert if evictions > baseline * 2.

james: thanks all. leaving channel.

nina: will check back in 30m or earlier if it flaps.

incident-bot: If p99 stays <= 700ms for 10m the incident will be marked resolved pending postmortem.
